documents.title: Concept of Operations (CONOPS): Requirements for a Mobile Robot Platform in MARS Research
documents.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
documents.summary: Defines the Concept of Operations (CONOPS) and operational use-case scenarios across 7 key platform areas: (1) Modularity and Extensibility, (2) Power Management, (3) Mobility and Manipulation, (4) Perception and Sensing, (5) Localization and State Estimation, (6) Multi-Agent Coordination and Communication, and (7) User Interface and Fleet Management.

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: Initial baseline release of Concept of Operations (CONOPS) specification (5-page PDF)
Established operational context and commercial-grade usability/accessibility objectives for MARS fleets
Defined Section 1 (Modularity & Extensibility) and Section 2 (Power Regulation, BMS Protection, Exchangeable Battery Module, Fleet Charging, Power On/Off Control)
Defined Section 3 (Holonomic/Closed-Loop Locomotion & Collaborative Manipulation), Section 4 (Environmental Perception & Reciprocal Collision Avoidance), and Section 5 (Pose Estimation)
Defined Section 6 (Peer-to-Peer Inter-Robot Communication & Decentralized Network Topology) and Section 7 (Fleet Monitoring, Onboard Display/Button UI, Status LEDs, Telemetry Logging)

documents.title: Stakeholder Needs and Requirements
documents.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
documents.summary: Identifies the 8 core stakeholder and research needs (RN-01 to RN-08) for a mobile robot platform supporting multi-agent experiments based on practical experience operating a four-robot team: fleet scalability, decentralized coordination, behavioral consistency, hardware/software adaptability, fleet-level endurance, environmental interaction, centralized telemetry/logging, and usability/reproducibility.

versions.author: Dhamdhawach Horsuwan
changes: Initial baseline release of Stakeholder Needs and Requirements specification (RN-01 through RN-08)
RN-01 & RN-02: Defined fleet scalability, cost-effectiveness, and decentralized inter-robot communication needs
RN-03 & RN-04: Established locomotion/sensing consistency and modular hardware/software extensibility needs
RN-05 & RN-06: Specified fleet-level power/charging operations, obstacle avoidance, and cooperative transport needs
RN-07 & RN-08: Defined centralized experimental monitoring/telemetry and cross-disciplinary reproducibility needs
